representation_hypothesis.frozen_hypothesis: the rigid coupler mount (centroid + full-turn-wrapped orientation) is the only representation the recorded instruments could score, so representation-driven rejection cannot be excluded from the records without a re-representation test

tested.hypothesis: a constant mounting-angle offset c alone (mounting vector (0,0)) re-represents the mount and could rescue candidates the records rejected
tested.test_method: pair-difference bounds on the per-pose gate inequalities: |wrap(theta_i + c - o_i)| <= 1.5 deg for every pose i implies the pose-to-pose coupler-orientation differences must cover the demanded differences within 2 x 1.5 deg; c cancels in every difference, so the swing requirement is invariant under H1

tested.hypothesis: a constant mounting vector v (with offset angle c) re-represents the mount and could rescue candidates the records rejected; the part centroid rides coupler point + R(theta + c) v
tested.test_method: v does not enter orientation, so the H1 swing bound is invariant under the full (v, c) class; for the position gate, a reverse-triangle necessary condition on the recorded per-target error magnitudes (|r_i - r_j| >= |e_i - e_j|, and gate-passing after any common offset requires |r_i - r_j| <= 2 x 1.5 mm), with the v-class rotational play bounded by the recorded per-pose orientation deviations from level and stated as the approximation error of the common-offset form

tested.hypothesis: a non-rigid mounting (a wrist, gripper compliance, a decoupled part orientation) could serve the demands
tested.test_method: out of class, recorded not tested: a mounting declaration is a constant (vector, angle, frame, lineage) over one rigid mount; a time-varying or compliant mount is a new mechanism family (the capability-step question, e.g. the dual-groove carrier), not a re-representation of the four-bar niche. B2 diagnoses the convention, not the family line

answer_reasons: Case study C (the recorded live blocker this diagnosis was commissioned on): the binding rejection -- orientation-dominant 36/36 -- is PROVEN invariant under the full rigid-mount re-representation class (H1 + H2). The demanded 180.000 deg swing between the handoff poses requires an unwrapped coupler swing of at least 177.000 deg after both pose tolerances; the pool's best free swing anywhere in any cycle is 156.452 deg; deficit 20.548 deg. A constant mounting angle cancels in pose differences and a mounting vector does not enter orientation, so no mounting declaration in the class rescues any candidate, pool-wide. Position fails independently (pool-best 11.65x tolerance; the D3a at-pose pairing is none for every candidate).

Case study B: the binding gate is position, and its rejection is proven no-rescue under the constant-offset class (H1 with the v-play set aside) for the pool's best candidate -- positive fixed_001, worst-pose 9.08 mm at 6.05x tolerance, pairwise magnitude spread 8.61 mm over the 3.00 mm necessary-condition threshold -- and for 6 of the 10 recorded frontier rows (spreads 4.26-10.76 mm). The recorded magnitudes cannot complete the exclusion for 4 of 10 frontier rows (spreads 1.15-1.49 mm; per-target residual directions are not recorded in the outcome tables), including the negative-direction pool-best; and under the full (v, c) class a nonzero mounting vector adds pose-dependent corrections the magnitudes cannot resolve (rotational play bounded by the recorded inter-pose orientation deviations, worst pair 17.75 deg). This caveat is recorded, scoped, and named with its follow-up; it does not touch the case C proof.

The records do contain representation artifacts -- the case B orientation gate as scored is representation-scoped (a constant mounting angle re-targets which coupler orientation counts as level), and the frontier holds candidates at a wrong-but-constant coupler angle (spreads 0.12-2.54 deg within the 3.00 deg threshold) whose orientation rejection is a pure mounting-angle artifact. The diagnosis detects them, and finds them non-binding: those candidates still fail the position gate, which binds deeper pool-wide (the recorded P2 refutation: qualification stops at position in every row).

The answer is therefore data-limited: the binding rejections in both recorded corpora are attributable to the pools' genuine capability limits -- for case C pool-wide under the full class, for case B for the pool's best candidate and 6/10 recorded frontier rows under the constant-offset class with the scoped caveat above. Per the frozen schema rule, recommended_convention is absent (present only for representation-limited or both); the rigid-mount convention as scored needs no amendment from this diagnosis.

evidence.claim: Swing invariance (case C): under any constant mounting-angle offset c and any mounting vector v, the flip demand requires an unwrapped coupler-orientation swing between the two handoff poses of at least 177.000 deg (180.000 deg demanded minus the two 1.500 deg pose tolerances); the pool's best free swing (recorded D3b, unwrapped full-cycle coupler-angle range) is 156.452 deg; deficit 20.548 deg.
evidence.method: pair-difference bound on the per-pose gate inequalities |wrap(theta_i + c - o_i)| <= 1.5 deg, differenced over handoff poses 1 and 3: c cancels, v does not enter orientation; minimum required swing = 180.000 - 1.500 - 1.500 = 177.000 deg, computed; compared against the recorded pool-max D3b 156.452 deg; deficit 177.000 - 156.452 = 20.548 deg, computed

evidence.claim: Binding class (case C): orientation-dominant 36/36; pool-best position error 11.65x the tolerance, pool-best orientation error 47.57x; the D3a at-pose pairing is none for every candidate (no candidate reaches both handoffs within position tolerance).
evidence.method: recorded digest verdicts D1-D4 of flip-station-failure-01 as recorded in that JOB.md's recorded outcome, consumed read-only; ratios as recorded

evidence.claim: Case C conclusion: the binding rejection is attributable to candidate data under the FULL rigid-mount re-representation class -- the orientation gate fails pool-wide invariantly (the swing bound), and position fails independently, so no (v, c) rescues any candidate.
evidence.method: conjunction of the two evidence rows above; no further data consumed

evidence.claim: Constant-offset position proof (case B): the recorded frontier's per-target position-error magnitudes prove no-rescue under a common offset for 6 of 10 rows -- pairwise magnitude spreads 8.61 / 7.86 / 9.32 / 9.36 / 10.76 / 4.26 mm each exceed the 3.00 mm necessary-condition threshold -- including the positive-direction pool-best fixed_001 (per-target errors 6.69 / 9.08 / 0.47 mm, worst-pose 9.08 mm at 6.05x tolerance).
evidence.source_data_point: case-B locator (no content sha256 recorded; pre-emitter record -- see data_points[1].locator)
evidence.method: reverse-triangle necessary condition: gate-passing after any common offset requires |r_i - r_j| <= 2 x 1.5 mm for every pose pair, and |r_i - r_j| >= |e_i - e_j| on the recorded magnitudes, so a pair spread above 3.00 mm proves no common offset passes all gates; spreads computed from the recorded per-target errors of the ten frontier rows

evidence.claim: Case B caveat: the remaining 4 of 10 recorded frontier rows (positive bridge_release_002; negative bridge_release_001 / bridge_trust_001, a duplicate-lineage pair, and bridge_trust_002) have spreads 1.15-1.49 mm at or below the threshold, so no-rescue is not provable from the recorded magnitudes; the negative-direction pool-best (worst-pose 10.45 mm at 6.97x) is among them. Under the full (v, c) class a nonzero mounting vector adds pose-dependent corrections whose rotational play is bounded by the recorded inter-pose orientation deviations from level (worst pair bound 17.75 deg, fixed_003: 9.72 + 8.03 deg); magnitudes alone cannot resolve them.
evidence.source_data_point: case-B locator (no content sha256 recorded; pre-emitter record -- see data_points[1].locator)
evidence.method: the same necessary condition read on both branches; the v-class play bound = 2|v| sin(dtheta/2) with dtheta bounded by the sum of the two largest recorded per-pose orientation deviations of the row; recorded as a scoped limitation with the follow-up named in docs/b2-answer.md

evidence.claim: Detected representation artifact, non-binding (case B): the orientation gate as scored is representation-scoped (a constant mounting angle re-targets which coupler orientation counts as level), and the frontier holds candidates at a wrong-but-constant coupler angle -- orientation spreads 0.12-2.54 deg within the 3.00 deg threshold for 9 of 10 rows (e.g. bridge_trust_001 positive: 6.15 / 6.40 / 6.42 deg) -- whose orientation rejection is a pure mounting-angle artifact. Every such row still fails the position gate, so the artifact is non-binding; the record also shows the genuine article (fixed_003 positive: orientation spread 3.35 deg over the threshold, no constant angle rescues it).
evidence.source_data_point: case-B locator (no content sha256 recorded; pre-emitter record -- see data_points[1].locator)
evidence.method: orientation spreads computed from the recorded per-target orientation errors against the 2 x 1.5 deg threshold; the c-retargeting argument is definitional (part orientation = coupler orientation + c under the rigid mount)

evidence.claim: Overall: the binding rejections in both recorded corpora are attributable to the candidate data. Case C is closed pool-wide under the full class; case B is closed for the pool's best candidate and 6/10 recorded frontier rows under the constant-offset class, with the scoped caveat above whose named follow-up (a direction-resolved re-representation re-score over the recorded corpora, read-only, the frame-sweep precedent) would close the remainder. The caveat does not touch the case C proof.
evidence.method: conjunction of the evidence rows above
